subject: R Distance error "All models failed to fit!"

messages.author: 7f87f78f0cd24437
messages.subject: R Distance error "All models failed to fit!"
parts:
Dear All,

 

I am working with some bird point count data, collected in a variety of habitats. I'm still at the early stages of distance sampling with this dataset and thought that I would try some basic pooled CDS analyses to get a sense of it all, before stratifying by habitat or trying some MCDS. However, I've run into some early issues and I would really appreciate some advice.

 

I have a lot of detections, but there is some definite heaping going on.

 

 

R Distance will fit models to the data as is, without binning, but the pdf plots look quite strange (I assume because of the heaping);

 

ds(DATA, truncation = 150, transect = "point", key = "hn", adjustment = NULL)

 

 

Therefore I wanted to try some binned analyses. However, when I bin the data, R Distance won’t run and just produces an error;

 

Columns "distbegin" and "distend" in data: performing a binned analysis...

Fitting half-normal key function

 

All models failed to fit!

 

Error in ds(DATA, truncation = 150, transect = "point", key = "hn", adjustment = NULL) :

  No models could be fitted.

 

This happens with both half-normal and hazard-rate models. I have tried the analyses with varying bin widths, but always get the same outcome. In searching this list, I found a thread from 2016 which suggested it was an issue with the mrds package at the time. I have made sure to update all of my packages, so I don’t think it is the same problem.

 

Am I missing something obvious? Any help would be really appreciated!

 

Thank you,

Tom

Tom:

Can't diagnose why you have fitting problems with your binned data without knowing how you did your binning.  Granted, you are going to have difficulty with the data set given the rounding your plots show.

Built a simple test case (with line transect data shipped with the Distance package) to demonstrate there is nothing inherently impossible about fitting detection functions to binned (line transect) data.

library(Distance)
data(minke)
minke_cuts <- create.bins(minke[!is.na(minke$distance),], c(0,.1,.2,.3,.4,.5,1,1.5,2))
sss <- ds(minke_cuts)
plot(sss)

parts:
Dear All,
Eric was able to solve my problem, see messages below. Essentially, one needs to truncate the data _before_ binning.
I was able to then fit a model without an error and the pdf graph looks as expected. See attached.
Many thanks to Eric!
Tom
11:24 AM (39 minutes ago)

Tom,

Another fictitious data set; this one highlights the problem:

hmm <- abs(rnorm(100, 0, 150))
fake <- data.frame(Region.Label="Eric", Area=100, 
                     Sample.Label=rep(seq(1,10),each=10), 
                     Effort=rep(seq(1,10), each=10), distance=hmm)
fake.cuts <- create.bins(fake, c(0,10,20,30,40,50,75,100,150,200,300,400,500,1000))
fake.OK <- ds(fake.cuts)
fake.FAIL <- ds(fake.cuts, truncation=200)

fake.trunc <- fake[fake$distance<=200, ]
fake.trunc.bin <- create.bins(fake.trunc, c(0,10,20,30,40,50,75,100,150,200))
fake.trunc.OK <- ds(fake.trunc.bin)

Code works for first call to ds() without trunctation, but fails with second ds() call where truncation is specified.  Third call to ds() works when truncation occurs prior to binning.




Dear Eric,


Thank you for responding so promptly. I have tried using the 'create.bins' function as per your code, but I get the same error message;

> DATA.binned <- create.bins(data = DATA, cutpoints = c(0,48,70,110,150,200,400))

> ds(DATA.binned, truncation = 150, transect = "point", key = "hn", adjustment = NULL)


I've tried a variety of cutpoints, but it always results in the same error. So I don't think that it is an issue with the way I was creating the bins. Presumably it is a problem with my dataset, but I am at a loss to work out what it could be. I know that it is hard to say without seeing the data, but have you any guesses?

Thanks,
Tom
